title: Arctic vs Antarctic
keyIdea: The Arctic and the Antarctic are both icy and cold, but they are opposites. The Arctic, round the North Pole, is a frozen ocean with land all round it; people live there in towns, and polar bears hunt on the sea ice. The Antarctic, round the South Pole, is a huge continent of land covered in thick ice, with ocean all round it; penguins live there, it is even colder, and nobody lives there all year, only scientists who visit.
familyTip: Put an ice cube in a glass of water and a second ice cube on a small upturned plate. Ask: which one is like the Arctic and which is like Antarctica? The floating cube is the Arctic: ice on top of water. The cube on the plate is Antarctica: ice on top of land.

visual.caption: Arctic or Antarctic? Drag each card, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drill through the ice at each pole, fill in the middle of each map, place buildings, fix two wrong posters and sort clue cards.

kid: The Arctic is at the top of the Earth, round the North Pole. The Antarctic is at the bottom, round the South Pole. Both are white, icy and very cold.

But they are opposites. Under the ice at the North Pole there is sea water. The Arctic is a frozen ocean, with land all round it. Under the ice at the South Pole there is rock. Antarctica is a huge piece of land, called a continent, with ocean all round it.
People live in the Arctic. They have towns, homes and schools. Nobody lives in Antarctica all the time. Scientists go there to work, then they go home.

Polar bears live in the Arctic. They walk on the frozen sea to hunt seals. Penguins live in the south, round Antarctica. A wild polar bear and a wild penguin never meet. Antarctica is the colder of the two.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This fits the National Curriculum in England. Key Stage 1 geography asks children to find the North and South Poles and the hot and cold areas of the world. Year 2 science covers living things and their habitats. Key words: Arctic, Antarctic, Antarctica, North Pole, South Pole, continent, ocean, sea ice, ice sheet.

The Arctic is the Arctic Ocean and the land round it. Most of that ocean is covered by floating sea ice a few metres thick. North America, Greenland, Europe and Asia ring it. Antarctica is the fifth-largest continent: rock under an ice sheet about 2 km thick on average, with the Southern Ocean all round it. It is high, dry land under ice, so it is much colder than the Arctic. The lowest air temperature ever measured, about −89 °C, was at Vostok Station in Antarctica.

Common mistakes: thinking the two poles are the same kind of place; thinking there is land under the North Pole; and thinking people live in Antarctica in towns. About four million people live in the Arctic. Antarctica has no one who lives there for good, only research stations. Another slip comes from cartoons that show polar bears with penguins. Polar bears live only in the Arctic. Wild penguins live only in the southern half of the world.

In the lab your child drags a drill down through the ice at each pole. They find sea water in the north and rock in the south. Then they fill in the middle of two maps, and place a house, a school, a shop and a science station. Next they move the wrong animal on each of two posters and sort six clue cards. Every action also has a button.

practice.prompt: What is under the ice at the North Pole?
practice.hint: Think about the drill. Did it hit water or rock in the north?
practice.explain: The Arctic ice floats on the sea. Under it there is sea water, so the Arctic is a frozen ocean.

practice.prompt: Which animal lives in the Antarctic?
practice.hint: Penguins live in the south. Polar bears and walruses live in the north.
practice.explain: Emperor penguins live round Antarctica. Polar bears and walruses live in the Arctic.

practice.prompt: A penguin group has {a} penguins. {b} more penguins waddle over. How many penguins now?
practice.hint: Start at {a} and count on {b} more.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b}. There are {=a+b} penguins on the Antarctic ice.

practice.prompt: {n} polar bears are on the sea ice. {k} bears walk away. How many are left?
practice.explain: {n} − {k} = {=n-k}. {=n-k} polar bears are still on the frozen Arctic sea.

practice.prompt: Where can you find towns where families live all year?
practice.hint: Does anyone live in Antarctica all the time?
practice.explain: People live in Arctic towns all year. In Antarctica there are only science stations, and people go home after a while.

choices: a huge, icy piece of land called a continent
pool.hint: The drill hit rock under the South Pole ice.
pool.explain: Antarctica is land covered in thick ice, with ocean all round it. That makes it a continent.

pool.prompt: Can a wild polar bear meet a wild penguin?
choices: no, they live at opposite ends of the Earth
yes, they play on the same ice
pool.hint: Polar bears live in the north. Where do penguins live?
pool.explain: Polar bears live in the Arctic and penguins live in the south, so in the wild they never meet.

pool.hint: One pole is thick ice piled high on land.
pool.explain: Both are very cold, but Antarctica is colder. It is high land under thick ice.

pool.prompt: The Arctic is an ocean with what all round it?
pool.hint: Think of the map: the middle is ocean. What is round the edge?
pool.explain: The Arctic Ocean has land all round it. Antarctica is the opposite: land with ocean all round it.

pool.prompt: A science station has {a} scientists. {b} more fly in for the summer. How many scientists now?
pool.hint: Put the two groups together: {a} and {b} more.
pool.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} scientists. They work in Antarctica for a while, then fly home.

pool.prompt: Mia says the North Pole and the South Pole are the same place. Is she right?
choices: no, one is at the top of the Earth and one is at the bottom
yes, they are next to each other
pool.hint: Think about the globe: top and bottom.
pool.explain: The North Pole is at the top of the Earth and the South Pole is at the bottom. They are as far apart as you can get.

pool.prompt: Why do polar bears need the frozen Arctic sea?
choices: they walk on the sea ice to hunt seals
pool.hint: What do polar bears eat, and where do they catch it?
pool.explain: Polar bears walk on the sea ice and catch seals at holes in the ice.

pool.prompt: {n} penguins are in a huddle. {k} go off to swim. How many penguins are still in the huddle?
pool.explain: {n} − {k} = {=n-k}. {=n-k} penguins stay in the huddle on the Antarctic ice.
